newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LECLAIR HAS 4 GOALS AS FLYER LEGION OF DOOM BURIES MONTREAL.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LECLAIR HAS 4 GOALS AS FLYER LEGION OF DOOM BURIES MONTREAL.

text.p: John LeClair had four goals and two assists as the newly reunited "Legion of Doom" line powered the Philadelphia Flyers to a 9-5 victory over the Montreal Canadiens Thursday.

LeClair completed his fifth career hat trick early in the second period and added his fourth goal late in the third. It was his first career four-goal game. LeClair had gone five games without a goal.

Eric Lindros and Mikael Renberg each added a goal and four assists as the Legion of Doom combined for six goals and 10 assists. The unit broke the team record for points in a game by one line, eclipsing the mark of 14 set by Darryl Sittler, Bill Barber and Ilkka Sinisalo on January 8, 1983.
"When things are clicking like that tonight, it's fun to get out there," LeClair said. "All three of us were going in the right direction. That made it fun to play."
"They were happy to be reunited, I guess. They had a tremendous night," Flyers coach Terry Murray said.
"The goals, the plays, the control time, the possession time in the offensive zone was outstanding."

Valeri Bure tallied twice for Montreal, which is winless in its last four games (0-2-2) and has just one victory in its last nine. The Canadiens have lost nine of 10 to Philadelphia since trading LeClair, Gilbert Dionne and Eric Desjardins to the Flyers in February 1995. Montreal also is 0-8-1 in its last nine visits to Philadelphia.
The nine goals were the most allowed by Montreal since its infamous 11-1 loss to Detroit on December 2, 1995 in what turned out to be goaltender Patrick Roy's last game with the Canadiens.
Tomas Vokoun surrendered six goals on 31 shots over the first two periods in his NHL debut and was replaced by Jose Theodore, who gave up three on 13 shots.
Ron Hextall stopped 24 shots for the Flyers, who improved to 3-1-1 in their last five games.
"The big line was awesome," he said. "When they play like that, with that jump in their legs, nobody can stop them. It's a fact of life."

In St Louis, Brett Hull scored two power-play goals and added a shorthanded tally for his second hat trick of the season and linemate Geoff Courtnall had a goal and three assists as the Blues beat the Dallas Stars 6-4.

The line of Hull, Courtnall and Pierre Turgeon combined for 11 points. Hull, who recorded his 28th career hat trick, has 14 goals and nine assists in his last 23 games, while Turgeon has 10 goals and 20 assists in his last 18 contests.

Turgeon and Scott Pellerin also tallied for St.Louis, which is 7-2-1 in its last 10 games. The Blues, who are 8-4-1 under coach Joel Quenneville, moved within one point of second-place Detroit in the Central Division.
Pat Verbeek, Bill Huard, Joe Nieuwendyk and Neal Broten scored for Dallas, which dropped to 5-3-1 in its last nine.

In Detroit, Martin Gelinas recorded his second career hat trick and Pavel Bure added four assists as the Vancouver Canucks defeated the Red Wings 7-4, denying coach Scotty Bowman his 1,000th career victory.
Trevor Linden had three assists for the Canucks, who snapped a three-game losing streak and a five-game skid on the road.
Detroit, which had allowed three goals or less in eight of its previous nine games, was blistered for 39 shots, including 17 in the opening period.
In Boston, Andrew Cassels scored a pair of third-period goals and Sean Burke made 41 saves as the Hartford Whalers snapped a three-game losing streak, 5-3 over the Bruins.
Cassels' goal with 15:05 to go in regulation snapped a 3-3 deadlock and he added an insurance tally on the power play with 9:48 remaining.
Rookie Kevin Brown and former Bruin Glen Wesley each had a pair of assists for the Whalers, who moved one point ahead of idle Washington for the final Eastern Conference playoff spot.
In Buffalo, red-hot Dominik Hasek made 32 straight saves after allowing an early goal and Donald Audette scored in the second period as the Sabres battled to a 1-1 tie with the Florida Panthers.
Hasek allowed Bill Lindsay's goal 2:06 into the game but shut down Florida the rest of the way, including three stops in overtime. He has allowed just six goals in his last five games.
Mark Fitzpatrick had 25 saves for Florida.
In Phoenix, Keith Tkachuk set up the tying goal midway through the third period and scored the game-winner with 69 seconds left in regulation as the Coyotes rallied past the Chicago Blackhawks 3-2.
Phoenix won for just the fourth time in 26 games when trailing after two periods.
Ethan Moreau and Brent Sutter had goals for the Blackhawks, who had their three-game winning streak snapped.
